history.p: Hartmann started working on this piano sonata sometime during the 1870s and end-dated the first two movements on 11 October 1876, nine years before the final version was published. During the following years it underwent a lot of changes, so that the two versions virtually assume the character of being two different works, (See JPEW III/1).

physDesc.physMedium: 6 bifolios. Written in pencil. Paper: 12 staves. Numerous delitions, corrections and additions. On the first nine pages scattered numbers from "11" to "16" can be found. On top of p. 7 is added "Rhapsodisk"; on pp. 9-10 is added "Vi-de No. 6". The six bifolios, of which one is erroneously divided into two single folios, are paginated 1 to 22 in a later hand; it is not clear whether this pagination reflects the correct order of the bifolios.

annot.p: Sketches for a number of unidentified works including the A minor Sonata. Both keys and thematic material indicate that the sketches belong to the early version of the Sonata.

titlePage.p: Kammerherre / Lehnsgreve Lerche Lerchenborg / tilegnet. / SONATE / (No 2) / for / PIANOFORTE / af / J.P.E. Hartmann. / Op. 80. / Forsynet med Fingersætning af Aug. Winding. / Forlæggerens Eiendom for alle Lande / KJÖBENHAVN. / Wilhelm Hansens Musik-Forlag.

annot.p: The first edition was published on the occasion of Hartmann's 80th birhday on 14 May 1885. A copy of this edition bears a dedication to the Danish Queen Louise, wife of King Christian IX, signed by Hartmann "Mai 1885" (DK-Kk, D 24). This also goes for the copy sent to the widow of the dedicatee, Count Lerche Lerchenborg, proving that the edition with the sentence “forsynet med Fingersætning…” (fingerings added), contrary to Dan Fog’s statement in his catalogue, is the original edition. In fact, both editions have fingerings in the music text itself.
